subject: Integration plan & tool-calling strategy for FinTect POC
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fintect.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15 15:10:00 +0000
Subject: Integration plan & tool-calling strategy for FinTect POC

Thanks again for the call this morning, Alex — good discussion and clear priorities. Below is a concise recap and proposed technical next steps so we can align the POC scope. I copied Aditya (solutions architect) and Ben (AE) for any follow-ups.

Recap (what you prioritized)
- Primary goal: replace manual reconciliation with embeddings + reranker for transaction anomaly grouping.
- Latency SLO: 300ms tail for single-transaction queries; batch scoring can be 1–2s.
- Data residency: US-only, retention 90 days.
- Auth: you prefer short-lived mTLS tokens integrated with your API gateway; SSO for engineers via Okta later.

Proposed integration approach (high level)
1) SDK & auth: onboard client via Redwood JS SDK (we'll provide a small starter package). Use per-service token for early POC, plan for MTLS/Okta SSO prior to production.
2) Routing: edge routing -> nearest Redwood region; set policy to route to quantized medium-cost model for user-facing queries, full-precision variant for nightly re-ranks.
3) Tool/function calling: define two tool categories: (A) internal connectors (DB read, enrichment) and (B) external services (fraud engine, accounting). We'll recommend function definitions with typed structured output (JSON schema) to reduce parsing errors.
4) Parallelization & error handling: allow parallel tool invocation for enrichment (fan-out up to 3), with circuit-breaker fallback to queue-and-retry for transient failures.
5) Embeddings/rerank: compute BM25-like candidate set then embed + cross-encoder reranker; keep embeddings in your VPC store during Private deployment if needed.

Attachments: I attached a short integration playbook and a sample tool-defs JSON that maps to the patterns we discussed.

Immediate asks for FinTect before the tech deep-dive:
- Share an anonymized sample of 1k transactions (CSV) and a schema (PII removed).
- Confirm whether mTLS is already terminable at your API gateway or needs edge setup.
- Confirm the list of services that need direct tool calls (e.g., fraudsvc, accountsvc).

Next steps (recommended cadence)
- Tech deep-dive (1.5h): Wed 11/18 — include your infra lead + our solutions team (Aditya).
- We’ll script a minimal starter app (JS SDK) and post a repo before the call.

Thanks — happy to iterate on the tool-def templates after you share the sample data.

Cheers,
Soojin
Soojin Lee | Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0187

Thanks — this is very helpful and aligns with what we discussed. Quick answers and a couple follow-ups inline.

- Sample data: we can share a 1k record anonymized CSV by EOD tomorrow.
- mTLS: our gateway currently terminates TLS; we can extend for mTLS but may need help with certificate rotation.
- Services to call: fraudsvc (internal), enrichmentsvc (external partner), ledger-svc (internal read-only).

Questions on tool patterns:
1) Parallel tool calls: are you recommending issuing all enrichment calls in parallel and aggregating results, or a staged approach (enrichment -> rerank -> enrichment on top results)? Our concern is hitting rate limits on enrichmentsvc (third-party) and also minimizing cost.
2) Error handling: if enrichmentsvc is down, can Redwood's runtime return a graceful partial response with flags for missing enrichment so our UI can surface degraded results?
3) Structured output: can you share one concrete example of a function definition for a reranker tool that returns a typed JSON output so we can wire it to our UI components?

We'll aim to be ready for Wed 11/18. Priya (cc) will own the infra coordination.

—Alex
Alex Turner | VP Product, FinTect Payments
alex.turner@fintect.com | +1 650-555-2244
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@fintect.com>
Date: 2026-11-16 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Integration plan & tool-calling strategy for FinTect POC

Alex — good questions. Answers below and I attached a one-page example tool-def for a reranker.

1) Parallel calls vs staged: recommendation = hybrid. For initial candidate enrichment, do parallel enrichment calls (fan-out) but cap concurrency to 3 and apply client-side rate limiting for the third-party enrichmentsvc. After candidate generation, run the reranker as a single cross-encoder call over the reduced candidate set to control cost and latency. This minimizes both external rate-limit exposure and embedding compute.

2) Error handling / graceful degradation: yes — Redwood supports structured error signaling in the runtime. You can define function outputs like {"results": [...], "warnings": ["enrichmentsvc_unavailable"], "partial": true}. The client SDK surfaces these fields so the UI can flag degraded results. We'll include a sample UI flagging pattern in the starter repo.

3) Example function definition (high level) — attached as fintect-sample-tool-defs.json. Key points:
- Input schema: {transaction_id, raw_text, candidate_ids?} (typed)
- Output schema: {ranked_ids: [string], scores: [float], metadata: {reason_codes: [string]}}
- Error fields: {partial: boolean, warnings: [string], retryable: boolean}

Immediate operational asks we still need from your side:
- Confirm the cert rotation window/ops owner for mTLS (so we can script short-lived cert issuance).
- Provide ETA for the anonymized CSV and a list of sample endpoints for enrichmentsvc and ledger-svc so Aditya can draft a mock connector.

Logistics: Wed 11/18 14:00 PT works on our side for the deep-dive — can you confirm? We'll open a shared repo and post a draft SDK starter and the example tool-defs before the call.

Short action items (owners)
- FinTect: share data + endpoints (Priya) — due 2026-11-16 EOD
- Redwood: repo + starter SDK + example tool-defs (Aditya) — due 2026-11-17 COB
- Schedule deep-dive and include infra/ops (Ben) — schedule link in Drive.

Thanks — I'll follow up with the repo link and a short checklist.

Best,
